verdict.line: You lose if you trade into his Q (Knuckle Down) empowered autos while backed against a wall; you win if you poke with Q (Blinding Dart) and E (Toxic Shot) from range and never let him land Facebreaker.

brief.thesis: This is a dead-even matchup (50.6% over 1426 games) that hinges entirely on positioning: Sett has zero ranged poke and no gap-closer, so every point of damage he deals has to come from you standing inside his E (Facebreaker, range 490) or Q (Knuckle Down) auto-attack range. Stay outside 490 units and auto-poke with E, and Sett simply cannot answer.

theirWindow.when: Facebreaker is up and you're near a wall or minion
theirWindow.what: Facebreaker pulls enemies standing on opposite sides of Sett together, stunning them (or slowing if only one side is hit). Don't let a minion or the lane wall sit on your far side while he's in range — back off until his E is on cooldown (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) before you commit to a trade.

yourWindow.when: right after Sett uses Facebreaker or Knuckle Down
yourWindow.what: With E down for up to 16s and Q down for up to 9s, Sett has no stun and no bonus-damage autos. Walk up and freely stack E (Toxic Shot) autos and land Q (Blinding Dart) — Blinding Dart also shuts off his empowered right-punch entirely for its duration since it removes his basic attacks.

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: The most-picked start (72.1% pick, 50% WR over 1379 games) — the extra sustain and AP let you win extended poke exchanges where Sett has no way to punish you for standing at range.

boots.why: Higher win rate and pick rate than Sorcerer's Shoes here (53.1% over 949 games) — the move speed lets you hold the 490-unit Facebreaker line while still landing E autos.

core.why: Attack speed and the on-hit proc stack E (Toxic Shot) poison faster, which is how you out-damage his passive regen
Burn damage over time overwhelms the health regen he gains from Pit Grit as he loses health in extended trades

runes.keystoneWhy: The 53.1%-winrate page's keystone rewards exactly the poke pattern this matchup calls for — three E autos from range trigger the burst proc before Sett can ever close the distance.

summoners.why: The dominant pick (89.7% pick rate, 50.9% WR) — Ignite cuts through the health regen Sett gains from Pit Grit when he's low, which is the main way all-ins slip away from you.

playing.title: Hold 490+ units at all times
playing.detail: Facebreaker only pulls enemies on opposite sides of Sett — if you're never in its 490 range, it physically cannot touch you. Let minions eat it instead.

playing.title: Blind before he commits
playing.detail: Q (Blinding Dart, 8s cooldown) removes his basic attacks entirely, which shuts off both his alternating-punch passive and the bonus damage from Q (Knuckle Down). Save it for the moment he walks in, not as a poke tool.

playing.title: Poke with E, never auto in melee range
playing.detail: E (Toxic Shot) has 680 range on-hit poison with no cooldown — get your autos off and step back immediately rather than trading autos face to face.

playing.title: Count his Facebreaker cooldown out loud
playing.detail: 16s at rank 1 down to 10s at rank 5 — once you clock when he last used it, you know exactly how long you have to freely stand closer and poke.

playing.title: Mushroom the brush and the wall gaps
playing.detail: R (Noxious Trap) has only a 1s cooldown — drop them in flank brush and along the wall he'd use to set up a Facebreaker pincer, both as vision and as a deterrent.

playing.title: Kite with W after every trade
playing.detail: W (Move Quick) gives passive move speed until struck — walk away after poking so he has to use Q's move speed just to catch up, buying you time before he's in range again.

playing.title: Respect The Show Stopper from level 6
playing.detail: R has a long 120s cooldown at rank 1, but it suppresses and slams you regardless of blind or peel — don't overextend right after he's used Q and E together, since that's when he's baiting the ult.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the ability breakdowns, timing windows, and trade patterns are my own tactical read of those numbers.
